definition.name: dead-code-elimination
definition.purpose: Remove unused operations, stores and private functions while retaining observable effects.
definition.tradeoffs: Usually reduces execution and size; compressed bytes can differ. Off retains optional dead-code work, not mandatory reachability and language lowering.

definition.name: constant-folding
definition.purpose: Evaluate bounded known operations and calls, propagate constants and consider literal representations.
definition.tradeoffs: Spends proof work to remove runtime work. Larger literals can hurt codec size; representation alternatives compete with full bytes. Off also vetoes root-string forwarding.

definition.name: inlining
definition.purpose: Replace proved calls with their bodies to expose simplification and remove call overhead.
definition.tradeoffs: Can increase text and compilation work. Shared removal-only inlining also needs dead-code-elimination; target implementations need target-compaction. Off vetoes all optional inlining.

definition.name: scalar-replacement
definition.purpose: Replace proved private object storage with independent values.
definition.tradeoffs: May remove allocations and fields but add locals or longer text. Escape, identity, initialization and capture proofs remain mandatory; off keeps the aggregate representation.

definition.name: call-specialization
definition.purpose: Specialize proved private function signatures and transport of product arguments.
definition.tradeoffs: Additional proofs and candidates can remove allocations or argument handling; more parameters can cost bytes. On permits competition only where every call is known.

definition.name: helper-sharing
definition.purpose: Compatibility name for optional parameterized helper sharing; no implementation is currently available.
definition.tradeoffs: Explicit on reports unavailable and does not alter output. Mandatory runtime helpers remain language lowering; this flag does not control them.

definition.name: target-compaction
definition.purpose: Permit optional target-tree cleanup, statement spellings and output families.
definition.tradeoffs: Adds formation and search work; spelling wins depend on the objective. Semantic subfamilies also need their own permissions. Off keeps mandatory lowering and independently permitted structural search.

definition.name: identifier-mangling
definition.purpose: Assign short hygienic names to private lexical bindings.
definition.tradeoffs: Usually reduces bytes without runtime work; names affect codec repetition. Off retains source naming and disables dependent naming trials; public-name contracts always apply.

definition.name: property-mangling
definition.purpose: Try coherent short names for proved private fields, including reuse across unrelated types.
definition.tradeoffs: Requires observation and inheritance proofs and extra formation/judgments. Preserved or reflected keys keep their names. Independent of lexical mangling; off vetoes cached and direct assignments too.

definition.name: string-pooling
definition.purpose: Share repeated literal strings or numbers through bindings.
definition.tradeoffs: Introduces bindings and reads; repetitive literal bytes can already compress well. Structural computed-string pooling additionally needs constant-folding. Off vetoes pooling in every route.

definition.name: string-array-packing
definition.purpose: Represent string arrays as delimited text decoded with split under pristine-builtins assumptions.
definition.tradeoffs: Can save bytes while adding decoding and allocations. Version 3 requires explicit on, including callable sites; legacy auto permits startup sites at effort 16 only. Off vetoes packing at all levels.

definition.name: startup-reconstruction
definition.purpose: Permit constant-table encodings with startup decoders.
definition.tradeoffs: Trades startup CPU/storage for possible delivery savings and extra search. Version 3 requires explicit on at every effort; legacy auto grants it at 16. Does not permit recurring decoding or string-array packing.

definition.name: recurring-reconstruction
definition.purpose: Compatibility name for recurring table reconstruction; no implementation is currently available.
definition.tradeoffs: Explicit on reports unavailable. String-array-packing owns its own callable-site risk and is not enabled by this flag.

definition.name: naming-search
definition.purpose: Explore lexical allocation styles, name reuse and local refinements under the selected objective.
definition.tradeoffs: Spends rendering and codec work for possible byte savings without intended runtime work. Effort schedules bound exploration; off keeps the baseline allocator.

definition.name: naming-alphabet
definition.purpose: Try alternative hygienic naming alphabets as joint name assignments.
definition.tradeoffs: May rename the whole artifact and add expensive codec trials for small or absent savings. Naming-search and identifier-mangling must remain permitted; off preserves their other strategies.
